_readme: Persistent fetch-failure ledger for the Las Azules S2 media sweep routine. Sweeps must read this before attempting any body fetch on a candidate URL and skip anything currently in cooldown, rendering the skip on the sweep evidence line. failCount tracks consecutive full fallback-chain failures (WebFetch AND Firecrawl scrape both failed in the same attempt). Three consecutive full-chain failures sets cooldownUntil to 30 days out. After cooldown expires, the URL gets one retry (WebFetch then Firecrawl); success resets failCount to 0 and clears cooldownUntil, failure restarts the 30-day cooldown. A separate category, permanentSkip with a skipReason, marks URLs that are fetchable but excluded for an editorial reason (for example a syndicated republication of a story already in data.json under a primary outlet). permanentSkip entries are skipped regardless of cooldownUntil and must never be treated as, or logged as, a fetch failure. See LEMA-9620 for origin, LEMA-9619 for the incident that motivated this file, and LEMA-9621 for the permanentSkip category. Two standing editorial rules, adopted LEMA-9642 (CEO ruling on LEMA-9641), apply to every sweep going forward and must not be re-escalated: (1) No proxy, inferred, or approximated dates ever enter data.json. A crawler artifact like this ledger's firstSeen timestamp is never a substitute for a real, sourced publish date -- not even with a disclaimer in the excerpt, because sorting and the dashboard KPIs read ts, not the excerpt. If no real publish date can be recovered (WebFetch AND Firecrawl both exhausted), the candidate is permanentSkip with skipReason "editorial_undateable" and reviewable: true, never added with a substitute date. (2) Social-candidate relevance gate, separate from and prior to any dateability check: vendor, supplier, crew-personal, and fan-repost accounts are not media coverage and must be skipped as permanentSkip on relevance grounds (skipReason "editorial_vendor_promo" for a vendor/supplier company account, "editorial_personal_repost" for an individual crew-personal or fan-repost account) regardless of whether a date could be found. Publisher, outlet, and editorial-brand accounts are media coverage and are evaluated normally, dateability included. reviewable: true (used on editorial_undateable entries only) marks a permanentSkip entry as genuine coverage omitted solely for lack of a real date, distinct from editorial_redundant_syndication (we already have the story) and editorial_vendor_promo/editorial_personal_repost (not coverage at all, dateability irrelevant). It is queryable only, for a future manual date lookup; it implies no dashboard or UI surfacing. A third standing rule, adopted 2026-09-06 (CEO ruling on LEMA-9761, implemented in LEMA-9762), applies going forward and must not be re-escalated: (3) no un-ledgered exclusions. Any decision to exclude a candidate from data.json must be written to this ledger as a permanentSkip entry in the same run the decision is made; a decision recorded only in a run comment or deliverable document does not persist, because the next sweep cannot see it. An exclusion must use one of the existing skipReason values above. Agents must not invent a new exclusion ground mid-run: if no existing skipReason fits a candidate, the candidate is included in data.json that run and a new issue is opened escalating the proposed category, rather than being excluded on an invented ground. Two scope clarifications travel with this rule: first-party promotional and BTS video produced by the studio or platform itself (trailers, "inside look" pieces, cast interview clips, press releases, official show pages) is media coverage under Rule B like any other official show/network account content, evaluated normally for dateability and duplication, not a candidate for a new editorial skip category. There is no publish-date floor on candidates: coverage is never excluded, under any rule, on the grounds that it predates Season 2, and Season 1 era coverage is in scope on the same terms as Season 2 coverage. A fourth standing rule, adopted 2026-09-10 (CEO ruling on LEMA-9880, implemented in LEMA-9883), applies going forward and must not be re-escalated: (4) Rule A applies retroactively, plus two guardrails. Rule A governs what ts means, not when an entry was written or which sweep run committed it: an entry that violates Rule A today violates it regardless of vintage, and there is no grandfathering for entries already in data.json. Rule C does not block retroactive remediation: Rule C governs how an exclusion is recorded (ledgered, in the run where the decision is made, using an existing skipReason), not when the candidate was first seen. A retroactive removal of an already-published entry satisfies Rule C when the data.json removal and the matching fetch-blocklist.json permanentSkip entry land in the same commit, because the remediation run is the run where the decision is made. Guardrail one, ledger precedence: before writing any permanentSkip entry to this ledger, check whether that same URL is already present in data.json. If it is, this ledger wins: remove the data.json entry in the same commit that adds the permanentSkip entry, rather than leaving a live feed entry that a permanentSkip entry silently contradicts. Guardrail two, future-ts guard: any candidate or existing data.json entry whose ts is later than the sweep's run date is an automatic Rule A violation, a publish date cannot be in the future, and must never be committed; an existing entry found with a future ts must be flagged and remediated under this rule (removed and ledgered in the same commit), not left in place. A fifth standing rule, adopted 2026-09-10 (CEO ruling on LEMA-9923, implemented in LEMA-9924), applies going forward and must not be re-escalated: (5) piracy and unauthorized-distribution gate, separate from and prior to any dateability check: a candidate is permanentSkip with skipReason "editorial_piracy_or_unauthorized_distribution" when both hold -- the page is on-topic for the show, and its primary function is supplying or linking to unauthorized copies of the title rather than reporting on, reviewing, or promoting it. Signals: download or torrent/magnet links, "ENLACE VIP"/"ENLACE FREE" style link tiers, an embedded full-episode player, release-quality labelling in the title (720p, 1080p, WEB-DL, HDTV), a synopsis blurb that exists only as an SEO wrapper around the links. Dateability is irrelevant to Rule E exactly as it is to Rule B: a piracy listing with a perfect sourced publish date is still not coverage. Rule E applies retroactively on the same logic Rule D established for Rule A: it classifies what an entry is, not when it was committed, so there is no grandfathering, and Rule C is satisfied when the data.json removal and the matching permanentSkip entry land in the same commit. reviewable is false or omitted on these entries -- reviewable: true means genuine coverage omitted solely for lack of a date, and these are not coverage at all, same posture as editorial_vendor_promo and editorial_personal_repost. The skipNote must record what is hosted, the claimed quality tier, the page publish date, and that it is an unauthorized-distribution listing. Four scope limits travel with this rule and must not be stretched: legal-availability guides ("where to watch" articles, JustWatch/Reelgood-style legal aggregators, official platform pages) are coverage and are evaluated normally; low-quality or SEO-farm editorial is still editorial, Rule E is about function, not production values; Rule E does not apply to social candidates at all, including YouTube -- trailer uploads, clip reposts, and channel overviews stay under Rule B's account-type gate; and ambiguity routes to Rule C, not to Rule E -- if a page has both real editorial content and unauthorized links, or you cannot tell, include it and escalate, never resolve ambiguity by stretching Rule E. A sixth standing rule, adopted 2026-09-10 (CEO ruling on LEMA-9751, implemented in LEMA-9927), applies going forward and must not be re-escalated: (6) listing/database gate, for on-topic and fetchable candidates that carry no written editorial content about the show: a candidate is permanentSkip with skipReason "editorial_listing_or_database" when it is a TVDB/IMDb-style episode listing row, an EPG or programming-grid page where the show is one row in a daily schedule, or a bare directory placeholder page for an episode that has not aired. Test: strip the metadata table or schedule grid from the page; if nothing written about the show remains, it is Rule F. Explicitly NOT Rule F, and must be left alone: an article about the release schedule is written journalism about the show and is coverage, not a data row -- the line is prose-about-the-show versus a data row, not the word "schedule" appearing in the URL or title. Three entries in data.json are the named near-miss cases and must never be reclassified under Rule F: Just Jared's episode-schedule/finale-date piece (ts 20260907), Fiction Horizon's "streaming schedule and what time it lands" piece (ts 20260819), and Film Book's Apple TV+ August schedule roundup (ts 20260725). reviewable is false or omitted on Rule F entries -- these are not coverage at all, same posture as editorial_vendor_promo and editorial_personal_repost. A seventh standing rule, adopted 2026-09-10 (CEO ruling on LEMA-9751, implemented in LEMA-9927), applies going forward and must not be re-escalated: (7) off-topic false-positive gate: a candidate is permanentSkip with skipReason "editorial_off_topic_false_positive" when it is about a different show, person, or topic entirely and surfaced only as a broad-query match. This is not an editorial judgment, it is a relevance miss, and it is ledgered for exactly one reason: so the sweep stops re-fetching the same non-qualifying URL every two hours. The skipNote on a Rule G entry must state what the page is actually about -- "off-topic" alone is not auditable and a wrong off-topic call would be invisible without it. reviewable is false or omitted on Rule G entries for the same reason as Rule F. Rule C still governs ambiguity for both Rule F and Rule G: if you cannot tell whether a page has real editorial content about the show, include it in data.json and escalate a new issue, never resolve the ambiguity by reaching for Rule F or Rule G. Both rules are forward-only as adopted -- a targeted scan of live data.json on 2026-09-10 found no existing entries of either class, so no remediation task was opened; if a future sweep encounters an existing entry that plainly fails Rule F or Rule G, Rule D's retroactivity logic applies (remove from data.json and add the permanentSkip entry in the same commit) without a fresh escalation.
